title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Provisions on the Supervision of Enforcement Cases and Two Other Systems for Enforcement Work
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Provisions on the Supervision of Enforcement Cases and Two Other Enforcement Work Systems

Fa Fa [2006] No. 11

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The following three enforcement work systems are hereby issued to you for diligent implementation: the Provisions on the Supervision of Enforcement Cases (Trial Implementation), the Provisions on the Management of Enforcement Funds and Property (Trial Implementation), and the Measures for the Filing and Archiving of People's Court Enforcement Documents (Trial Implementation).

Please promptly report any issues encountered during implementation to this Court.

May 18, 2006

Provisions on the Supervision of Enforcement Cases (Trial Implementation)

To strengthen and regulate the supervision by higher-level courts over the enforcement cases of lower-level courts, these Provisions are formulated in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and relevant judicial interpretations, and in light of the practical experience of people's courts in enforcement work.

Article 1 The Supreme People's Court shall supervise the enforcement cases of local people's courts at all levels. High People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts shall supervise the enforcement cases of people's courts within their respective jurisdictions.

Article 2 Where a party reports that a lower-level court has engaged in passive enforcement or that a case has remained unresolved for a prolonged period, and the higher-level court deems the report to be true, it shall urge the lower-level court to promptly take enforcement measures, or to conclude the case within a specified time limit.

Article 3 Within ten days after receiving a petition reporting enforcement issues of a lower-level court, the higher-level court shall prepare a supervision letter for cases meeting the conditions for supervision, and shall transmit the letter together with relevant materials to the lower-level court. Under special circumstances, the higher-level court may require the lower-level court to report immediately, or may dispatch personnel for on-site supervision.

Upon receiving the supervision letter from the higher-level court, the lower-level court shall designate specific personnel to handle the matter.

Article 4 The lower-level court shall submit a written report to the supervising court on the case handling progress or proposed handling opinions within the time limit specified by the higher-level court.

Article 5 For an enforcement case under supervision by a higher-level court, the court being supervised shall, in accordance with the requirements of the court at the next higher level, promptly prepare a case supervision letter and transmit it together with relevant case materials to the enforcement court. The court being supervised shall, before the expiration of the time limit set by the court at the next higher level, submit a written report on the handling of the supervised case to the court at the next higher level, together with relevant materials.

Article 6 Where a lower-level court fails to report the work progress or case outcome within the prescribed time limit, the higher-level court may issue a reminder, or may directly retrieve the case files for review, designate another court to handle the case, or elevate the level of enforcement.

Article 7 After receiving the written report from the lower-level court, if the higher-level court considers the proposed handling opinions of the lower-level court to be inappropriate, it shall issue a written opinion and notify the lower-level court accordingly. The lower-level court shall handle the matter in accordance with the opinion of the higher-level court.

Article 8 Where a lower-level court believes that the handling opinion of the higher-level court is erroneous, it may request reconsideration from the higher-level court in accordance with relevant provisions.

For a case in which the lower-level court requests reconsideration, the higher-level court shall form a separate collegial panel to conduct a review. If upon review the original handling opinion is found to be erroneous, it shall be corrected; if the original handling opinion is found to be correct, the higher-level court shall prepare a letter urging the lower-level court to handle the matter in accordance with the original handling opinion.

Article 9 For an enforcement case under supervision by a higher-level court, if the lower-level court, without justifiable reason, fails to report the work progress or case outcome within the prescribed time limit, or refuses to implement or passively implements the handling opinion of the higher-level court, and fails to correct the situation even after a reminder from the higher-level court, the higher-level court may issue a notice of criticism within its jurisdiction, and shall pursue the liability of the relevant court or responsible person in accordance with relevant provisions.

Article 10 These Provisions shall take effect from the date of promulgation.

Provisions on the Management of Enforcement Funds and Property (Trial Implementation)

To strengthen the management of enforcement funds and property of people's courts and to protect the lawful rights and interests of parties, these Provisions are formulated in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and relevant judicial interpretations, with reference to relevant financial management regulations, and in light of the actual circumstances of enforcement work.

Article 1 The enforcement funds and property referred to in these Provisions are the financial assets and property that, in accordance with the law, should be managed by the people's court during the enforcement process.

Article 2 The financial departments of people's courts at all levels shall open dedicated accounts for enforcement funds, and shall implement dedicated management and dedicated payment of enforcement funds.

The enforcement organs and financial departments shall divide responsibilities, cooperate with each other, and supervise each other.

Article 3 The financial department shall register the receipt and payment of enforcement funds on a case-by-case basis and establish detailed accounts. The enforcement organ shall designate specific personnel to set up ledgers for the receipt and payment of enforcement funds, and shall maintain detailed records for each case. The case handler shall register the flow of enforcement funds for each enforcement case and include such records in the case file.

Article 4 During compulsory enforcement, enforcement funds may be directly delivered by the person subject to enforcement to the applicant for enforcement, or may be directly transferred from the account of the person subject to enforcement to the account of the applicant for enforcement. However, for enforcement funds that are disputed or need to be redistributed, or for other circumstances where the people's court deems it necessary to first deposit them into the dedicated account for enforcement funds, such funds shall be transferred into the dedicated account.

Article 5 Where the person subject to enforcement directly pays cash or negotiable instruments to the court, the enforcement personnel shall, together with the person subject to enforcement, deliver the cash or negotiable instruments to the financial department of the court, which shall issue a receipt.

Article 6 Where during enforcement it is truly necessary for enforcement personnel to directly receive cash or negotiable instruments on behalf of the court, at least two enforcement personnel shall be present, shall immediately issue a receipt to the payer, and shall record the receipt in the笔录 and have it signed by the payer.

The recipient shall, within one working day after returning to the court, transfer the funds or deposit the relevant funds into the dedicated account for enforcement funds.

Article 7 Where a people's court entrusts an auction institution to auction the property of the person subject to enforcement, the auction entrustment letter shall require that the bidder or buyer directly remit the deposit or auction price into the dedicated account for enforcement funds of the court. The remittance shall indicate the remitting unit, the name of the auction institution, the name of the person subject to enforcement, and the case number.

Article 8 The day after the enforcement funds are received into the account, the financial department shall notify the enforcement organ of the receipt. The enforcement organ shall, within five days, inform the parties to the case of the time and amount of receipt and other relevant information.

Article 9 After the enforcement funds are received into the account, the enforcement court shall, within one month, calculate the enforcement costs and enforcement funds, and shall promptly notify the applicant for enforcement to go through the procedures for withdrawing the funds. If the payment needs to be deferred, a written explanation of the reasons shall be provided before the expiration of the time limit and submitted to the responsible leading official of the court for review and approval.

Article 10 When payment from the dedicated account for enforcement funds is required, the enforcement personnel shall fill out the relevant approval form for payment of case funds, together with the following materials, and submit it to the enforcement bureau director or the responsible leading official of the court for approval, and then hand it over to the financial department for processing.

(1) The effective legal document and the case filing approval form;
(2) Relevant proof that the funds have been received into the account;
(3) Valid identification of the applicant for payment. Where another person is entrusted to receive payment on behalf, a special power of attorney shall be issued to the court;
(4) Receipts or explanations for fees already withheld or to be withheld.

When the financial department pays enforcement funds, it shall conduct a careful review in accordance with relevant financial management regulations.

Article 11 Before paying enforcement funds to the applicant for enforcement, the people's court shall, in accordance with the law, deduct the unpaid litigation costs for enforcement and the actual expenses incurred during enforcement.

Article 12 When delivering enforcement funds to a party, the people's court shall simultaneously collect and verify the receipt issued by the party.

Article 13 Sealed or seized property held by the people's court shall be designated to specific personnel for storage, shall be properly kept, and no person shall use it without authorization.

Article 14 After the enforcement court releases the measures of sealing, seizing, or freezing property, it shall promptly return the property.

Article 15 When a case handler is transferred from the enforcement organ, he or she must, at the same time as handing over the case, also hand over the enforcement funds, property, and related materials. Where the handover of enforcement funds and property is unclear, the transfer procedures may not be processed.

Article 16 The use, interception, misappropriation, embezzlement, or private distribution of enforcement funds and property is strictly prohibited. Violators shall be held accountable in accordance with relevant provisions.

Article 17 During the implementation of these Provisions, each High People's Court may formulate implementation rules based on actual needs.

Article 18 These Provisions shall take effect from the date of promulgation.

Measures for the Filing and Archiving of People's Court Enforcement Documents (Trial Implementation)

I. General Provisions

Article 1 To strengthen the filing and archiving of enforcement documents, these Measures are formulated in accordance with the Archives Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court Archives Management Measures, and other relevant provisions, and in light of the actual circumstances of people's court enforcement work.

Article 2 For the purposes of these Measures, "enforcement documents" refer to all types of documentary materials related to a case that are formed during the enforcement process of a people's court.

Article 3 The following enforcement cases handled by a people's court shall be included in the scope of filing and archiving:

1. Enforcement cases directly accepted by the court;
2. Cases where enforcement has been elevated to a higher level or cases designated for enforcement;
3. Cases entrusted for enforcement;
4. Cases of enforcement supervision, requests for instructions, and coordination;
5. Cases where reconsideration is applied for;
6. Other enforcement cases.

Article 4 Enforcement cases shall be uniformly filed by the case filing tribunal, and shall be numbered by case type.

Each enforcement case must have a single case number. All judicial documents, official correspondence, telegrams, and other judicial documents, as well as the filing, archiving, and preservation of enforcement documents formed from case acceptance to case closure, shall use the case number assigned at the time of case acceptance.

Where a suspended enforcement case is resumed, a new case number shall not be assigned, and the original case number shall continue to be used.

Article 5 The responsible clerk shall be responsible for collecting, organizing, and filing the enforcement documentary materials. The responsible enforcement judge or enforcement officer and the department head shall be responsible for checking the quality of the case file and supervising the responsible clerk to ensure timely archiving.

II. Collection of Enforcement Documentary Materials

Article 6 After an enforcement case is accepted, the responsible clerk shall immediately begin collecting the various documentary materials related to the case and commence the filing work.

Article 7 Enforcement documentary materials shall comprehensively and truthfully reflect the entire enforcement process and specific circumstances.

Article 8 Service of legal documents shall be accompanied by a service receipt attached to the file.

Where legal documents sent by mail are returned, the receipt for the registered mail item and the returned envelope with the postal service's change of address or return note shall be attached to the file.

Where legal documents are served by public announcement, the original announcement and its attachments, the newspaper page containing the announcement, or a photograph of the posted announcement shall be attached to the file.

Article 9 Receipt and payment materials for enforcement funds and property must be attached to the file, including: the stub of the receipt for collecting enforcement funds and property; the receipt issued by the party after delivery or return of funds or property; the notice of fund transfer; receipts for litigation costs for enforcement and actual expenses withheld by the court; the ruling on debt satisfaction by transfer of property and materials concerning the delivery process of the transferred property; and copies of receipts for funds or property delivered after both parties have entered into a settlement agreement.

Article 10 For enforcement legal documents included in the file, in addition to the copies bound in the file, three copies for each document shall be attached to the file and placed in the pocket at the bottom of the file for future use. For other documentary materials, generally only one copy shall be retained (except for materials with instructions from leading officials).

Article 11 Enforcement documentary materials included in the file shall retain the originals. Where originals cannot be provided, one copy may be retained, but the reason for the absence of the original shall be noted. Where enforcement personnel, in the exercise of their functions, obtain evidentiary materials related to the case through excerpts or reproductions, the source and date shall be noted, and the material shall be signed by the person handling the matter, and stamped with the seal of the providing unit.

Article 12 The following documentary materials generally shall not be archived:

1. Envelopes or work materials without evidentiary value;
2. Duplicate materials with identical content;
3. Copies of laws, regulations, and rules;
4. General drafts of legal documents (not final versions);
5. Materials unrelated to the case.

Article 13 After the case is concluded, the enforcement personnel shall carefully check whether all documentary materials for the entire case have been collected. If any legal document is found to be incomplete, it shall be supplemented promptly.

III. Arrangement of Enforcement Documentary Materials

Article 14 The sequence of arrangement of enforcement documentary materials shall follow the process of the enforcement proceedings and the chronological order of formation of the documents, while also taking into account the organic connections between the documentary materials.

Enforcement case files shall be created separately as main files and auxiliary files, based on the principles of facilitating confidentiality and convenience of use. Cases without content that is not suitable for public disclosure may dispense with an auxiliary file.

Article 15 The sequence of arrangement of documentary materials in the main file of an enforcement case:

1. Case file cover; 2. Table of contents of the file; 3. Case filing approval form; 4. Application for enforcement; 5. Basis for enforcement; 6. Notice of case acceptance, notice of burden of proof, and service receipt; 7. Receipts for case acceptance fees and actual expenses; 8. Enforcement notice, notice of property declaration, and service receipt; 9. Identity documents of the applicant for enforcement and the person subject to enforcement, business registration materials, identity certificate of the legal representative, power of attorney, and letter from the law firm; 10. Evidentiary materials submitted by the applicant for enforcement, the person subject to enforcement, and third parties; 11. Transcripts of inquiries, investigations, hearings, and enforcement, as well as materials obtained by the people's court; 12. Documentary materials concerning the adoption, release, or revocation of compulsory enforcement measures (including inquiries, sealing, freezing, deduction and transfer, seizure, appraisal, auction, sale, search, summons for detention, fines, detention, etc.); 13. Original of the ruling on adding or changing the subject of enforcement; 14. Original of the ruling on compulsory enforcement; 15. Enforcement settlement agreement; 16. Evidentiary materials concerning the performance of the enforcement settlement agreement; 17. Ruling on debt satisfaction by transfer of property and related materials; 18. Rulings on suspension of enforcement, termination of enforcement, or refusal to enforce, and enforcement certificates; 19. Receipts and delivery certificates for enforcement funds and property, and related approval materials; 20. Approval form for extension of the enforcement period; 21. Case closure report and case closure approval form; 22. Service receipt; 23. Endorsement sheet; 24. Exhibit envelope; 25. Bottom of the file.

Article 16 The sequence of arrangement of documentary materials in the main file of an enforcement supervision case:

1. Case file cover; 2. Table of contents of the file; 3. Case filing approval form; 4. Petition for enforcement supervision; 5. Original enforcement ruling; 6. Identity documents of the parties or identity certificate of the legal representative, power of attorney, and letter from the law firm; 7. Evidentiary materials provided by the parties; 8. Transcripts of hearings and investigations; 9. Supervision letter; 10. Written report of the enforcement court; 11. Supervision result or relevant ruling; 12. Case closure report and case closure approval form; 13. Service receipt; 14. Endorsement sheet; 15. Exhibit envelope; 16. Bottom of the file.

Article 17 The sequence of arrangement of documentary materials for an enforcement coordination case:

1. Case file cover; 2. Table of contents of the file; 3. Case filing approval form; 4. Report requesting coordination and related evidentiary materials; 5. Coordination letter; 6. Report of the coordinated court and related evidentiary materials; 7. Minutes of the coordination meeting; 8. Review report of the case handler; 9. Minutes of the collegial panel's deliberation of the case; 10. Records and meeting minutes of the enforcement bureau (division) studying the case; 11. Records and meeting minutes of the judicial committee studying the case; 12. Coordination opinion letter; 13. Case closure report and case closure approval form; 14. Endorsement sheet; 15. Exhibit envelope; 16. Bottom of the file.

Article 18 The sequence of arrangement of documentary materials for an enforcement case requesting instructions:

1. Case file cover; 2. Table of contents of the file; 3. Case filing approval form; 4. Report requesting instructions and related evidentiary materials; 5. Review report of the case handler; 6. Minutes of the collegial panel's deliberation of the case; 7. Records and meeting minutes of the enforcement bureau (division) studying the case; 8. Records and meeting minutes of the judicial committee of the court studying the case; 9. Request for instructions or report to the higher-level court; 10. Approval opinion; 11. Case closure report and case closure approval form; 12. Endorsement sheet; 13. Exhibit envelope; 14. Bottom of the file.

Article 19 The sequence of arrangement of documentary materials in the main file of an enforcement reconsideration case:

1. Case file cover; 2. Table of contents of the file; 3. Case filing approval form; 4. Petition for reconsideration; 5. Original decision; 6. Identity documents of the applicant for reconsideration, identity certificate of the legal representative, power of attorney, and letter from the law firm; 7. Evidentiary materials provided by the applicant for reconsideration; 8. Transcripts of hearings and investigations; 9. Reconsideration decision; 10. Case closure report and case closure approval form; 11. Service receipt; 12. Endorsement sheet; 13. Exhibit envelope; 14. Bottom of the file.

Article 20 The sequence of arrangement of documentary materials in the auxiliary file of various enforcement cases:

1. Case file cover; 2. Table of contents of the file; 3. Notes on case file review; 4. Enforcement plan; 5. Materials or transcripts of internal exchanges of opinions between the case handler and relevant departments; 6. Internal requests for instructions and approvals concerning the case; 7. Instructions from higher-level courts or from leading officials of relevant units on the case; 8. Review report of the case handler; 9. Minutes of the collegial panel's deliberation of the case; 10. Records and meeting minutes of the enforcement bureau (division) studying the case; 11. Records and meeting minutes of the judicial committee studying the case; 12. Signed version of the legal document; 13. Other materials not suitable for public disclosure; 14. Endorsement sheet; 15. Exhibit envelope; 16. Bottom of the file.

IV. Filing and Binding of Enforcement Documents

Article 21 After systematic collection, organization, and arrangement of the enforcement documentary materials of the people's court, each page shall be numbered. Page numbers shall be written in Arabic numerals, with the number written on the upper right corner of the front side and on the upper left corner of the back side. Pages without writing on the back side shall not be numbered. The case file cover, table of contents, endorsement sheet, exhibit envelope, and bottom of the file shall not be numbered.

Article 22 The writing and signing of enforcement documentary materials, including the file cover, must use carbon ink, blue-black ink, or be printed by computer. Where documentary materials are written with red ink, blue ink, pencil, ballpoint pen, or other easily faded writing instruments that are not conducive to long-term preservation, a copy of the material shall be attached. Faxed documentary materials that need to be archived must be photocopied, with the photocopy archived and the fax not archived.

Article 23 The case file cover must be filled in completely in accordance with item requirements, with neat, standardized, and clear handwriting. The case number on the cover must be consistent with the case number in the file. In the "Case Type" column, "Enforcement" shall be filled in. In the "Cause of Action" column, the cause of action as confirmed by the basis for enforcement shall be filled in. In the "Parties" column, the information shall be filled in accurately and completely, without abbreviations or omissions. The dates of case acceptance and closure shall be consistent with the records in the file. In the "Enforcement Subject Matter" column, the subject matter amount applied for enforcement shall be filled in. In the "Enforcement Result" column, the amount already enforced or other circumstances shall be filled in. In the "Adjudicating Authority" column, the authority that issued the effective legal document shall be filled in. In the "Case Closure Method" column, depending on the circumstances, "Voluntary Performance," "Compulsory Enforcement," "Termination of Enforcement," "Enforcement Settlement," or "Refusal to Enforce" shall be filled in. In the "Date of Case Closure" column, the date of approval of case closure shall be filled in.

Article 24 The table of contents of the file shall be filled out item by item in the order of the documentary materials. Each documentary material shall be assigned one sequence number.

Article 25 For the page number of the table of contents, except for the last item where the start and end page numbers shall be filled in, only the start page number shall be filled in.

Article 26 The endorsement sheet of the file shall consist of the following items: description of the status of the file, filer, checker, acceptor, and date of filing.

In the "Description of the Status of the File" column, information on damage, modification, supplementation, removal, or destruction of the documentary materials in the file shall be filled in. The "Filer" column shall be signed by the filer. The "Checker" column shall be signed by the responsible enforcement judge or enforcement officer. The "Acceptor" column shall be signed by the person receiving the file from the archives department. The "Date of Filing" column shall be filled in with the date on which the filing is completed.

Article 27 The binding of case files must be firm, neat, and aesthetically pleasing, facilitating storage and use.

The thickness of each volume should not exceed 15 mm. If there are too many materials, they should be bound in separate volumes in sequence. Each volume of the case file shall be paginated starting from "1". The case file shall be bound flush at the bottom and right side, with three holes and one thread, and the length shall be approximately 180 mm. A seal shall be affixed over the knot of the binding thread at the bottom of the file, stamped by the file compiler.

Article 28 Before binding the case file, a comprehensive inspection of all documentary materials shall be conducted. Incomplete materials shall be completed; damaged, faded, or smeared materials shall be repaired or reproduced.

The paper used for materials within the file shall be A4 office paper as the standard. Excessively large paper shall be trimmed and folded; excessively small paper or paper with too narrow a binding margin shall be backed with additional paper.

Materials in foreign languages or minority languages shall be accompanied by a Chinese translation.

Envelopes kept for evidentiary purposes of date examination shall be retained in their original form, opened, flattened, and backed with additional paper.

Metal objects are strictly prohibited from being left inside the case file.

V. Filing and Preservation of Execution Case Files

Article 29 Enforcement personnel shall properly preserve the execution case file and prevent it from being damaged, omitted, or lost.

Article 30 The responsible clerk shall complete the binding of the execution case file within one month after the case is reported as concluded, and shall submit it to the relevant department or responsible person for verification of whether it meets the conditions for archiving. Those that pass inspection shall be archived immediately. Those that do not pass shall be remedied in a timely manner.

The execution case file shall be archived within three months after the case is reported as concluded.

Article 31 The enforcement organ shall register the archiving status of execution case files in a roster. Archived cases must have a receipt procedure from the archives department.

Article 32 Cases with suspended enforcement may be centrally preserved by the enforcement organ, and shall not be kept by enforcement personnel.

Article 33 The retention period for execution archives shall be determined by the archives management department in accordance with relevant provisions.

Article 34 No materials may be extracted from an archived case file. If it is truly necessary to add materials, the consent of the archives management personnel shall be obtained, and the matter shall be handled in accordance with the requirements for file compilation.

Article 35 Personnel who violate these Measures by failing to file in a timely manner, arbitrarily extracting documentary materials from case files, or damaging, omitting, or losing case file materials shall be dealt with accordingly in accordance with relevant provisions, depending on the seriousness of the circumstances.

VI. Supplementary Provisions

Article 36 In implementing these Measures, each Higher People's Court may formulate implementation rules based on actual needs.

Article 37 These Measures shall come into force on the date of promulgation.
